senses.gloss:
Kuntī
------------------------------------------
Among all the women characters of the Mahābhārata, कुन्ती, the मोथेर् of the Pāṇḍavas, impresses us as a noble and gentle lady, a personification of fortitude, even in the most troublesome periods of her life.
Known formerly as Pṛthā, the daughter of the king Śūra of the race of the Yadus (and a sister of Vasudeva, कृष्ण’s ड़थेर्) she was adopted by the king Kuntibhoja. Hence she acquired the name ‘Kuntī’ which stuck.
Once, as a girl, while attending upon the sage दुर्वासस् in her ड़थेर्’s होउसे, the sage, being pleased by her devoted service, taught her a special मन्त्र by which she could invite a god to come to herself to bless her with a child. Out of sheer curiosity, she tried it, inviting सूर्य or the Sun-god. As a result, a brilliant and valorous son was born to her. Being an unwed girl and afraid of calumny she left the baby floating in the nearby river after putting it in a wooden box. The box was recovered by one Adhiratha (the charioteer of धृतराष्ट्र) who along with his wife राधा, adopted him as his son and brought him up. This was कर्ण.
Kuntī was married to पाण्डु, the younger brother of the blind prince धृतराष्ट्र. Mādrī was her co-wife. Since पाण्डु was under a curse and could not get children in the normal way, कुन्ती revealed to him, about the gift of मन्त्र she had received from the sage दुर्वासस्. With पाण्डु’s permission she begot three sons (Yudhiṣṭhira, भीम and अर्जुन) and Mādrī too, with her help, gave birth to the twins—Nakula and सहदेव.
After the death of पाण्डु and Mādrī, she brought the five Pāṇḍavas to भीष्म, the grandsire, for bringing them up and for proper एदुचतिओन्.
She accompanied the Pāṇḍavas after they escaped from the arson of the inflammable होउसे built of lac, to the small town एकचक्रनगर. It was she who encouraged her son भीम to kill the demon Bakāsura, who was harassing the residents of that town.
When the Pāṇḍavas were banished to the forest after the second game of dice, she lived in the होउसे of विदुर, the minister of धृतराष्ट्र.
Before the कुरुक्षेत्र war, she met कर्ण, revealed the secret of his birth and advised him to join the Pāṇḍavas. (However कर्ण politely refused.)
After the war and युधिष्ठिर was crowned the king, she retired to the forest along with गान्धारी and धृतराष्ट्र. There she perished in a forest fire.
